body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38819
Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2668

## What changed

- Split DeepSeek-V4.1's C4 compressor pending C2 pair out of the heterogeneous SWA state component.
- Register C2 buffers at one FP32 row per item rather than one request ring per item.
- At the committed handoff boundary, send no C2 payload for even `N`; for odd `N`, map `p = N - 1` through each endpoint's own request slot and ring capacity.
- Add the distinct `dsv4_c2_state` wire component to Mooncake and NIXL, including exact index-cardinality checks and PP-aware layer slicing. This keeps incompatible legacy/full-ring layouts distinguishable instead of silently truncating them.
- Preserve the existing C128 request-state path and document the currently supported static DSpark PD scope.

## Reproduction and validation

The prepared base already contained the static DSpark PD candidate from upstream PR #38949. On that base, `get_dsv4_c4_state_indices` rejected a legal non-speculative ring size of 2 and represented `N=101` as five live rows; state registration multiplied each row size by the local ring capacity. The retained baseline evidence is in `reports/j-180e7a7f59ec/raw/baseline-c2-implementation.txt`.

Run:

```bash
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-180e7a7f59ec/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_backend_basic.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py
```

Result: 93 passed, plus 17 passed subtests. The regression covers unequal ring sizes, odd/even boundaries, wraparound, row-granular registration, the 12 KiB three-layer payload, and both transport helper suites.

A real GPU numerical check ran on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X. For `N=101`, source ring 2 and destination ring 8 mapped the pending logical position 100 to their independent physical rows. One 4096-byte FP32 row was copied for each of layers 2, 8, and 14; all values matched an independent CPU reference exactly and a neighboring destination row remained untouched. Raw output is retained under `reports/j-180e7a7f59ec/raw/`.

Pre-commit passed for every changed source, test, and documentation file. No native code changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable; the pinned Torch/ROCm stack was preserved.

## Incomplete / unverified parts of the source request

This is a verified candidate for the C2 boundary-transfer defect, not a claim that the complete upstream feature request is qualified.

- End-to-end DeepSeek-V4.1 PD + DSpark generation was not run. The prepared node is ROCm/MI350X, while the current DSpark implementation accepts CUDA or NPU only.
- No DeepSeek-V4.1 target and DSpark draft weights were available locally. The supplied tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify this architecture or DSpark semantics.
- Mooncake and NIXL were validated at the protocol/unit layer, not with a real multi-process or cross-node RDMA generation workload.
- Streaming, concurrent requests, chunked prefill, prefix hits, rejection paths, cancellation, slot reuse, actual speculative acceptance, throughput, and generation parity against a colocated V4.1 reference remain unverified end to end.
- Decode radix cache, dynamic/ragged verification, multimodal rebootstrap, and heterogeneous parallel layouts remain unsupported by the existing guarded static candidate.

The structured result and raw evidence are in `reports/j-180e7a7f59ec/`.
